title: Mexico’s Culture Secretary Proposes Zero Tax Rate for Small and Medium Bookstores; It Would Mean a Tax Benefit of Some 250 Million Pesos
author: Reyes Martínez Torrijos
content:
_This article by[Reyes Martínez
Torrijos](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Reyes%20Mart%C3%ADnez%20Torrijos)
originally appeared in the [September 9, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/09/cultura/claudia-curiel-
fortalecer-la-lectura-y-el-ecosistema-del-libro-ejes-para-impulsar-el-sector-
editorial), Mexico’s premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** Claudia Curiel de Icaza, head of the federal Secretariat of
Culture, explained in an exclusive interview with La Jornada the details of
the comprehensive policy for the book sector announced at a press conference
this Wednesday.

Amid a reduction in operations at Ediciones Era and in response to President
Claudia Sheinbaum’s instruction to review the matter, Curiel said that,
together with Paco Ignacio Taibo II, director of the Fondo de Cultura
Económica (FCE), they developed a proposal “in favor of reading and the book
ecosystem, which begins with the writer, the publishers, and the bookstores,
and reaches all the way to the reading public.”

The first measure in the set is “to request a **zero tax rate for small and
medium-sized bookstores**.” This proposal, the official reported, was included
in the Federal Revenue Law of the 2027 Economic Package that was submitted to
the Congress of the Union last Tuesday.

If the Legislature approves this provision, “which I think it will, because it
is a noble and important cause,” Curiel said, it would mean “a tax benefit of
between **200 and 250 million pesos** that will no longer be collected, but it
gives oxygen directly to the entire ecosystem of the sector and represents an
important relief for the independent and mid-sized effort.”

She said the zero rate for small and medium-sized bookstores, which was worked
out with the Secretariat of Finance and Public Credit and the Tax
Administration Service and was backed by the President, is part of “a
sustainable policy and not an ephemeral fix. In that sense, it means thinking
about a guild much broader than a single publisher.”

The official added that “Era is very important for its catalog, for having
Mexican writers and thinkers who are relevant in our history, but there are
many small and medium-sized publishers, very important ones, that could be in
the same situation.”

The second measure is the launch next week of a call for proposals from the
Secretariat of Culture, through the Vasconcelos Library and in collaboration
with the FCE, for the bulk purchase of books this year for an amount of **50
million pesos** directed at publishers.

“The call will be open for about two weeks, and then a plural reading
committee will be established to nourish the libraries and part of their needs
in science communication, the history of Mexico, literature, in short, several
areas that we will prioritize for the public.”

The third part is an amount from the Secretariat of Culture and the FCE of
between five and eight million pesos aimed at supporting small and medium-
sized state book fairs, “to decentralize and strengthen the different
territories in the area of reading and thus be able to diversify and
strengthen the different links.”

The fourth section of the comprehensive policy, which Curiel said had already
been in the works, includes the comprehensive rehabilitation of the
Vasconcelos Library, which in 2026 marks **20 years of operation** , with an
investment of 14 million pesos for infrastructure, services, connectivity, and
maintenance. Next year there will be a new phase of work at this venue.

The cultural promoter announced that from September 25 to 27 they will carry
out a program at the Vasconcelos Library, with talks, illustrators, sales of
books from independent publishers, concerts by Ricardo Gallardo, Tambuco,
Héctor Infanzón, and orchestras, as well as the participation of many
representative figures from the sector “to have a broad celebration of its 20
years with the launch of these actions.”

Curiel summarized: “President Claudia Sheinbaum gave Paco and me full backing
for this comprehensive policy to support the ecosystem of reading promotion,
publishers, circulation, and the strengthening of the collections of the
library network.”

She stressed, “I am very happy about a comprehensive policy like this, because
we are talking about an entire sector and not just a single publisher, above
all, about the smallest publishers, which are the ones that make an important
effort to keep going.”

> “We are talking about an entire sector and not just a single publisher,
> above all, the smallest publishers, which are the ones that make an
> important effort to keep going.”
>
> Claudia Curiel de Icaza, Secretary of Culture

The head of the Secretariat of Culture concluded that this is a set of
measures that is “sustainable and not an action in the face of a crisis that
merely mitigates a moment, but rather thinking about the health and
strengthening in the medium and long term, among many other things that can be
done, but that must continue to be worked on throughout the administration and
in collaboration with the FCE.”
